newsitem.title: USA: US judge sets arguments in ex-NASD employee's case.
newsitem.headline: US judge sets arguments in ex-NASD employee's case.

text.p: A federal judge said he will hear oral arguments May 30 on whether to dismiss a former NASD employee's charges that she was forced to resign because she blew the whistle on lax muni bond market enforcement by the group, lawyers for the employee said.

U.S. District Court Judge Leonard Wexler also said he will hear arguments May 30 on a related motion by the National Association of Securities Dealers to bar public access to court papers filed by the employee Theresa Carr, Carr lawyers Singer Zamansky said in a press statement.

Carr filed a $20 million damages lawsuit last September charging she was pushed out as senior compliance examiner in NASD's district 10 office in New York City because of her aggressive probe of "pay-to-play" in the muni market.
Among Carr's charges are that NASD district officials failed to pursue allegations that several bond firms made payments to Armacon Securities Inc. in return for bond business in recent years.

NASD on May 16 said it reached a final settlement with First Albany Corp. and its chief of muni bond operations concerning payments to Armacon, which had political connections to former New Jersey Gov. Jim Florio.
